_note: The event library. Each entry is one kind of thing that can happen. See docs/events.md for every field. Edit freely: change a number, a sentence or a rate; add an entry by copying one.

events.title: The gift season opens
events.headline: Shoppers begin to think about other people
events.story: Mid-November is when buying gifts stops being a distant idea. Browsing rises first, then baskets. Shops that photograph their stock well do better now than they will in the last week of December.

why.demand.all: Early gift buyers; December has its own monthly weight already.
why.demand.products.biscuit-tin: A tin is the safe gift.
why.demand.products.spare-sock: A sock is a gift you can post flat.
why.visits: People browse a month before they buy.

chatter: Browsing is up and baskets are not. Give it a week.
Somebody asked if the tin comes gift wrapped. It does not.

events.title: Black Friday week
events.headline: A week of discounts that shoppers have been told is a bargain
events.story: From the Monday before Black Friday to the Monday after, every shop announces a deal and every shopper compares them. Visits jump and so do questions about delivery dates. Couriers carry the heaviest week of their year.

why.demand.all: A well known national shopping week; the shop's own sale rules still decide how much of it we get.
why.no_delay: Couriers plan for this date with extra rounds, so parcels arrive on time; strikes, storms and fog are what make parcels late.

chatter: Everyone wants to know if it will arrive before Christmas.
The courier has stopped answering the depot phone. Typical.

events.title: The Christmas run-up
events.headline: Twenty-one days, and a good many gifts still to find
events.story: December is the biggest month for any gift shop, and the first three weeks are when most of it happens. The shop's monthly weight already doubles trade, so this adds only the gift shape inside it. People ask more questions about wrapping, dates and returns.

why.demand.all: Small extra on top of the December monthly weight.
why.demand.products.spare-sock: Stocking filler.
why.demand.products.biscuit-tin: A tin is the safest gift in the shop.
why.demand.products.trophy: The 'Well done.' trophy is an office-party favourite.
why.contact_rate: Gift buyers ask about dates and returns.

chatter: Every other email is 'will it arrive by the 24th?'
Stock check on the tins, please. They are going.

events.title: Last posting week
events.headline: Last posting dates arrive; parcels begin to queue
events.story: The final week before the courier's Christmas cut-off sees the busiest sorting offices of the year. Parcels that normally take two days take three. Customers write in, politely at first.

why.contact_rate: Customers worry about the cut-off date.
why.supplier_late_chance: Suppliers deliver into the same queue.
why.no_delay: Couriers add rounds for the last posting days, so parcels still arrive on time; the rush shows up as more questions, not late parcels.

chatter: The cut-off is the cut-off. Say it kindly, say it once.
Three people have asked if it will arrive 'by Christmas'. It is the 17th.

events.title: Christmas Day
events.headline: The country puts down its phones and picks up its sprouts
events.story: Nobody orders on Christmas Day and nothing is delivered. Browsing drops to a trickle until the evening. The couriers are shut until the 27th.

why.demand.all: The shop sells less on the day itself; people are with family.
why.visits: Almost nobody browses until the evening.
why.carrier_delay_days: No deliveries today or on Boxing Day.

chatter: Closed. The out-of-office is on.
No parcels move today. That is not a delay, that is Christmas.

events.title: Boxing Day
events.headline: Sales begin; so do returns
events.story: The shop is not open to the post but the website is. Shoppers with gift vouchers and spare time browse for bargains. The first returns of unwanted presents start to arrive.

why.visits: Shoppers use vouchers and spare time.
why.no_delay: Couriers plan for this date with extra rounds, so parcels arrive on time; strikes, storms and fog are what make parcels late.

chatter: First wave of 'it does not fit' emails.
The sale shoppers are back and they have read the small print.

events.title: The days between
events.headline: The week nobody can name a day of
events.story: From the 27th to New Year's Day, offices are shut and nobody knows what day it is. Orders slow right down. The couriers work a reduced timetable.

why.demand.all: People are away and the gift rush is over.
why.no_delay: Couriers plan for this date with extra rounds, so parcels arrive on time; strikes, storms and fog are what make parcels late.

chatter: Is it Tuesday? Nobody here is sure.
Quiet. Do not read anything into it.

events.title: New Year resolutions
events.headline: A nation resolves to be better organised, for about three weeks
events.story: In the first weeks of January, people tidy, plan and buy equipment for the new person they intend to be. Stationery and bags sell well. By late January the resolution has usually faded.

why.demand.all: Gift money has run out; the monthly weight already allows for it.
why.demand.products.daypack: A fresh start with a better bag.
why.demand.products.pocket-jungle: Greenery to go with the tidy desk.

chatter: Pens are moving. The diaries must have come out.
January: where everyone is going to start properly.

events.title: Valentine's Day
events.headline: Romance, scheduled for the 14th
events.story: In the fortnight before the 14th, gift shoppers look for something that says they thought about it. A sock, strangely, can say that. Next-day delivery requests rise on the 12th and 13th.

why.demand.all: Gift shoppers, mostly the day before.
why.demand.products.spare-sock: A thoughtful gift for someone who loses socks.
why.demand.products.biscuit-tin: A tin of biscuits is a safe romantic gesture.
why.demand.products.pocket-jungle: A small living thing that is not a rose.

chatter: Last orders for the 14th are tomorrow. Say so on the site.
The Spare Sock is somehow a romantic object. Do not question it.

events.title: February half-term
events.headline: Schools close for a week and households look for things to do
events.story: For a week the children are at home and the grown-ups would like them to be occupied. Small, odd, hands-on things sell better. The shop sees more families browsing in the afternoons.

why.demand.all: A small family boost.
why.demand.products.paper-aeroplane: A thing to do with an afternoon.
why.demand.products.pocket-jungle: A project for a rainy day.

chatter: More afternoon browsing than usual.
The aeroplanes have had a good week.

events.title: Pancake Day
events.headline: The nation flips a pancake and misses
events.story: Shrove Tuesday is a single day of cooking and mild disaster. Food and kitchen treats get a small lift. The shop sees more chilled and snack orders that evening.

why.demand.all: A small general lift from a food-themed day.
why.demand.categories.food: People are thinking about food and treats.

chatter: Biscuit orders are up. Something about pancakes.
Everyone is flipping something today.

events.title: Mother's Day run-up
events.headline: Ten days to find something better than flowers
events.story: Mothering Sunday falls three Sundays before Easter. The week before it is the second busiest gift week of the spring. Delivery by Saturday is the thing everybody asks about.

why.demand.all: Gift buyers for one fixed day.
why.demand.products.biscuit-tin: A tin of biscuits is the standard gift.
why.demand.products.pocket-jungle: A living gift that lasts longer than flowers.
why.demand.products.spare-sock: A practical gift for a practical mother.

chatter: Will it be there by Saturday? Please say yes, please be right.
Tin stock check. It is that week.

events.title: Spring clean
events.headline: The clocks go forward and so do the cupboards
events.story: When the evenings lengthen, people tackle the loft. Moving boxes, packing and tidying products sell better. The shop sees more bulk buying of packing material.

why.demand.products.bubble-wrap: People pack up what they are keeping.
why.demand.products.spare-sock: Odd socks get sorted out of the drawer.
why.demand.categories.desk-home: A tidy desk is easier to sell yourself on.

chatter: More bubble wrap this week. The loft is open.
Somebody ordered six. For packing, they say.

events.title: The clocks go forward
events.headline: An hour is lost and nobody can find it
events.story: At one in the morning the clocks skip to two. Sunday is a slightly shorter day and everyone is slightly late. A handful of customers ask whether the order cut-off has moved.

why.demand.all: A short, groggy day.

chatter: Did the cut-off move? No. We have not moved. The clock has.
Sunday was short. That is all.

events.title: The tax year ends
events.headline: Businesses spend what they were going to spend by the fifth of April
events.story: Offices and small firms buy the last of their budgets before the tax year ends. Orders from businesses go up a little and ask for proper invoices. Gift orders stay about normal.

why.demand.all: A small lift from business buyers using up budgets.
why.demand.products.trophy: Office awards need doing before the year ends.
why.contact_rate: Business buyers ask for VAT invoices.

chatter: Three invoice requests this morning. It is that time of year.
Business orders are up. Put the invoices on top.

events.title: Easter weekend
events.headline: Four days off, and the post takes four days with it
events.story: From Good Friday to Easter Monday, the couriers do not run. Families go away and orders dip, though snacks and picnic food rise. Chocolate and biscuits are the best performers.

why.demand.all: People travel and shops close.
why.demand.products.emergency-sandwich: Picnic food for the long weekend.
why.no_delay: Couriers plan for this date with extra rounds, so parcels arrive on time; strikes, storms and fog are what make parcels late.

chatter: Parcels will go out Tuesday. That is the long weekend, not a fault.
The tin is the Easter gift of choice.

events.title: Early May bank holiday
events.headline: A long weekend with a forecast
events.story: The first Monday in May gives the country a three-day weekend. If the weather is kind, they go outdoors. Couriers do not collect on the Monday.

why.demand.all: People are out and about.
why.no_delay: Couriers plan for this date with extra rounds, so parcels arrive on time; strikes, storms and fog are what make parcels late.

chatter: Bank holiday. Orders will move on Tuesday.
A good weekend for stones, apparently.

events.title: Exam season
events.headline: Revision is at its peak; so is the need for a decent pen
events.story: From the middle of May to the end of June, students sit exams and families wait for results. Pens, bags and snacks sell better. Paper aeroplanes sell to those who ought to be revising.

why.demand.products.one-good-pen: A good pen for the exam hall.

chatter: Pens again. The exams are on.
The aeroplane is not revision. We are not saying that out loud.

events.title: Late May bank holiday
events.headline: The second long weekend of the month; the barbecue is fired
events.story: The last Monday of May is a bank holiday and half term for most schools. Families head to the coast and the shop sees more outdoor buying. Parcels sit at the depot until Tuesday.

why.demand.all: People are away.
why.demand.products.ice-by-post: Cold drinks, in a sensible week.
why.no_delay: Couriers plan for this date with extra rounds, so parcels arrive on time; strikes, storms and fog are what make parcels late.

chatter: Same story as the first May holiday, only warmer.
Ice orders are up. The weather looks decent.

events.title: Father's Day run-up
events.headline: A tie is no longer the right answer
events.story: On the third Sunday in June, fathers are given gifts. The shop sees a ten-day run-up. The trophy, which says 'Well done.', is the favourite and nobody knows why.

why.demand.all: Gift buyers for one fixed day.
why.demand.products.trophy: Telling a father he did well is the whole gift.
why.demand.products.one-good-pen: A pen is a proper present.
why.demand.products.boombox-mini: Something to play music on in the shed.

chatter: Trophies are going. 'Well done, Dad' is a whole present.
Last order for the 21st is Thursday. Write that on the page.

events.title: The summer holidays begin
events.headline: Six weeks off school; the country goes outside
events.story: From the end of July to the start of September, families travel and the weather decides everything. Outdoor, travel and picnic goods lead sales. The shop's monthly weight already allows for the August dip in office orders.

why.demand.all: People are away.
why.demand.products.starter-puddle: A cheap amusement for the garden.

chatter: Quiet on the office side, busier on the daypack.
Stones are up. Rivers are open.

events.title: Exam results days
events.headline: The envelopes are opened; the congratulations begin
events.story: In the second half of August, exam results arrive and families celebrate or console. A trophy that says 'Well done.' is the obvious purchase. Biscuits follow, for either mood.
chatter: Trophy up on results day, as expected.
People write 'for after the results'. We prefer not to ask which kind.

events.title: August bank holiday
events.headline: The last long weekend before the term begins
events.story: The final bank holiday of the summer sends the country to the coast one more time. Couriers close on the Monday and half the orders wait until Tuesday. The first back-to-school shoppers appear.

why.demand.all: People are away.
why.demand.products.skimming-stones: A last trip to the water.
why.no_delay: Couriers plan for this date with extra rounds, so parcels arrive on time; strikes, storms and fog are what make parcels late.

chatter: Orders move Tuesday. It is a bank holiday, not a fault.
Start of the bag season.

events.title: Back to school
events.headline: Uniform, lunchbox, and a pen that works
events.story: In the last week of August and first of September, parents buy everything their children need. Bags, pens and packed lunches dominate. It is the busiest fortnight of the autumn for everyday goods.

why.demand.all: A general lift from parents buying.
why.demand.products.one-good-pen: Every child needs a pen that works.

chatter: Bags and pens. Here we go.
Daypacks at risk of selling out. Check the count.

events.title: The clocks go back
events.headline: An extra hour in bed; an earlier dark
events.story: The clocks go back and the evenings close in. People spend more time indoors and online. Home and desk goods sell a little better in the weeks that follow.

why.demand.products.indoor-helmet: Low beams are harder to see in the dark.

chatter: An extra hour of sleep and the evening traffic is up.
Dark by five. Orders are up by six.

events.title: October half-term
events.headline: A week at home, a week of small amusements
events.story: Late October brings a week off school. Parents look for something to do. The shop sees family browsing and small gift buying ahead of Halloween.

why.demand.all: A small family boost.
why.demand.products.paper-aeroplane: Something to do on a wet afternoon.

chatter: Afternoon browsing again. It must be half-term.
More aeroplanes than usual.

events.title: Halloween
events.headline: A night of mild fright and sweets
events.story: For the week before the 31st, shoppers look for costume extras and treats. Padded headgear sells as part of a costume. Biscuits are bought for the callers.

why.demand.all: A general lift for seasonal browsing.
why.demand.products.indoor-helmet: A padded cap makes an excellent costume.

chatter: A helmet as a costume. We did not plan for that.
Treat tins. They will get through them.

events.title: Bonfire Night
events.headline: Fireworks, mist and a flask of something hot
events.story: On the fifth of November people gather outside in the cold. Warm snacks and biscuits sell. The evening dips for online orders and recovers on the sixth.

why.demand.all: People are outdoors, not at a screen.
why.demand.products.emergency-sandwich: A sandwich at a bonfire is an emergency.

chatter: Quiet tonight. Everyone is outside.
The sandwich as bonfire food. Good.

events.title: Postal strike
events.headline: Postal workers walk out; parcels pile up in sorting offices
events.story: Staff at the national postal service have stopped work over pay. Letters and small parcels are sitting in sorting offices. Shops that depend on the post are warning customers to expect delays.

why.visits: A few shoppers hold off ordering.
why.contact_rate: Customers ask where their order is.
why.carrier_delay_days: Parcels wait in sorting offices; about three days late.

chatter: Where is my parcel? Strike. Same answer, new tone.
Every second email today is about the post. Keep the reply short.
Tell them it is moving, just slowly.

events.title: A long postal dispute
events.headline: Postal dispute enters its third week
events.story: A pay dispute at the national postal service has run well past the first strike days. Rolling walkouts have left a backlog of parcels. Smaller shops are advised to send by a private courier where they can.

why.demand.all: Some customers wait until it is over.
why.visits: Browsing slows when delivery dates are uncertain.
why.contact_rate: A steady stream of where-is-it questions.
why.carrier_delay_days: A long backlog; parcels take about five days longer.

chatter: Three weeks of this. The template is worn out.
We are using the other courier where we can.
The backlog is bigger than the depot.

events.title: Postal go-slow
events.headline: Post is running a day behind, says service
events.story: The national postal service reports a staff shortage and says first-class mail is arriving a day late. No strike has been called. Shops are noticing the same thing from their own tracking.

why.carrier_delay_days: A staff shortage costs roughly a day.

chatter: Everything is a day late. Not a disaster, just annoying.
Tracking says 'delayed' on a hundred parcels.

events.title: Courier price rise
events.headline: Large courier raises its rates for the new year
events.story: One of the larger parcel couriers has announced an average price rise on business accounts. Small shops are told the change is unavoidable. Many will absorb it rather than lose customers.

why.costs.carrier: A typical annual courier increase of about eight percent.

chatter: The courier invoice is up again. I will do the sums.
Shipping cost per order has crept up. Check the margin.

events.title: Fuel price jump
events.headline: Fuel prices jump at the pumps
events.story: Petrol and diesel have risen sharply in a fortnight. Couriers say they will pass some of it on. Suppliers' vans cost more to run, too.

why.costs.carrier: Couriers add a fuel surcharge of about five percent.
why.costs.goods: Suppliers pass on a small transport cost.

chatter: Fuel surcharge on the invoice. Again.
Supplier says the van costs more. They are not wrong.

events.title: Courier hub fault
events.headline: Sorting hub fault leaves parcels in a queue
events.story: A parcel courier says a fault at its main sorting hub has delayed deliveries across the country. Engineers are said to be working on it. Parcels are moving again but slowly.

why.carrier_delay_days: A backlog of about two days while the hub catches up.

chatter: The courier's hub has a fault. Not ours, but ours to explain.
All 'delayed' parcels are from the same depot.

events.title: Courier driver shortage
events.headline: Couriers short of drivers as demand holds up
events.story: Parcel companies say they cannot find enough drivers. Some rounds are being doubled up and deliveries are slipping. The shortage is expected to last a few weeks.

why.carrier_delay_days: Doubled-up rounds cost about a day.

chatter: Drivers are short. The parcels are fine, just late.
Fewer 'out for delivery' updates than usual.

events.title: A cheaper courier arrives
events.headline: New parcel courier launches at lower rates
events.story: A new national parcel courier has opened for business and is pricing below the established firms. Small shops are being offered trial rates. The older couriers are said to be considering their position.

why.costs.carrier: A trial rate about five percent below the usual.

chatter: Cheaper rate offered. Read the small print first.
Margin on postage is better this month.

events.title: Port delays
events.headline: Container backlog at the ports delays imported goods
events.story: A backlog of containers is holding goods at several ports. Shops that import components or finished goods are warning of late stock. Prices of some items are creeping up.

why.supplier_late_chance: Imported stock arrives later than promised.
why.costs.goods: Suppliers add a small handling charge.

chatter: The supplier says the container is sitting at the port.
Restock date moved again. Update the site.

events.title: Transport strike days
events.headline: Transport strike days announced; roads busier
events.story: Rail and bus workers have called strike days this week. More people are at home or on the roads. Parcel vans are slowed by the traffic.

why.visits: More people working from home and browsing.
why.carrier_delay_days: Extra road traffic slows parcel rounds by about a day.

chatter: More browsing today. Everyone is at home.
A van was stuck for two hours. It will be late.

events.title: Fake parcel texts
events.headline: Fake delivery texts spread across the country
events.story: Police say a wave of fake delivery messages is going round, asking people to click a link to rebook. Real shops are seeing customers ask whether their own delivery notices are genuine. Everyone is told to check the sender.

why.contact_rate: Customers write in to check that a text is real.

chatter: No, we never ask you to click a link to rebook.
Is this text real? is the new where is my parcel.
Make the 'how we contact you' page easier to find.

events.title: Congestion in the capital
events.headline: Roadworks and a closure slow deliveries in the capital
events.story: A major road closure has put the city's delivery rounds well behind schedule. Couriers advise customers inside the ring road to allow a day more. The works are due to last about a fortnight.

why.carrier_delay_days: Rounds in the city run a day late.

chatter: Deliveries to the city are a day behind. Not ours.
Allow an extra day for the capital.

events.title: Heatwave
events.headline: Heatwave: the country discovers it owns no fans
events.story: Temperatures have passed thirty degrees for the third day. Shops report a run on cold drinks, ice and anything that goes in a lake. Chilled parcels are a worry for couriers.

why.demand.all: People spend the hot days outside.
why.contact_rate: Questions about whether chilled goods survive.

chatter: Ice by Post is on its third reorder. It is hot.
Someone asked if ice melts in the post. It does.
Fan sales: not our department.

events.title: Cold snap
events.headline: A cold snap grips the country; the pavements are slippery
events.story: Overnight temperatures have dropped below freezing and the forecast is for more. People are staying in. Parcels are being held back on icy roads.

why.demand.products.pocket-jungle: Indoor greenery for a dull week.
why.demand.categories.desk-home: People stay in and buy for the house.
why.visits: People are at home with a screen.
why.carrier_delay_days: Icy roads slow the rounds.

chatter: Ice by Post is not moving. Obviously.
Parcels held for the ice. Update the banner.

events.title: A week of rain
events.headline: It rains, and then it rains some more
events.story: A slow front has stalled across the country and forecasters have run out of words. Umbrellas sell; so do indoor amusements. Outdoor buying stops.

why.demand.products.skimming-stones: The rivers are over their banks.
why.demand.products.starter-puddle: A tray to hold the puddle you already have.

chatter: Umbrellas are selling. The Other one, of course.
Wet week, good week for the website.

events.title: A warm spring weekend
events.headline: First warm weekend of the year sends people outdoors
events.story: The temperature has jumped to twenty degrees and the park is full of pale people. Picnics and stones sell. The umbrella is forgotten for a day.

why.demand.products.ice-by-post: First cold drink of the year.

chatter: Stones and sandwiches. It must be spring.
The umbrella has a quiet weekend.

events.title: Storm in the south-west
events.headline: Storm batters the south-west; roads closed
events.story: A named storm has brought gales and flooding to the south-west. Several roads are shut and some villages have lost power. Couriers have stopped deliveries in the worst-hit areas until it passes.

why.demand.all: People are busy with the storm, not the shop.
why.demand.products.other-umbrella: Nobody sells umbrellas to a gale.
why.contact_rate: Customers ask where their order is.
why.carrier_delay_days: Roads closed; couriers stopped in the worst areas.

chatter: Parcels for the south-west are held. Tell them kindly.
Customers in the storm area are being very patient. Thank them.

events.title: Floods in the north
events.headline: Rivers burst their banks across the north
events.story: After a week of rain, several northern rivers have burst their banks. Streets are under water and deliveries are suspended. Householders are being warned to expect a long clean-up.

why.demand.all: Households focus on the clean-up.
why.demand.products.bubble-wrap: People pack what they can save.
why.carrier_delay_days: Roads and depots are under water.

chatter: Do not chase flooded customers. Offer to pause the order.
Deliveries to the north are paused. Put it on the site.

events.title: Snow on the moors
events.headline: Snow closes the moor roads
events.story: A heavy fall of snow has blocked roads across the high moors. Gritting lorries are working through the night. Shops in the hills are expecting a quiet week.

why.demand.all: People stay home.
why.demand.products.spare-sock: Dry feet.
why.demand.products.indoor-helmet: Slips on the ice at home.
why.carrier_delay_days: Roads are blocked until they are gritted.

chatter: The moor roads are shut. Parcels are held.
Socks are moving on the moors. Of course they are.

events.title: Card fees go up
events.headline: Payment processors raise their fees
events.story: Payment companies have announced higher charges on every card payment. Small shops have no choice but to accept the change. Some are adding a small surcharge, others are absorbing it.

why.costs.card_fee: A ten percent rise in the percentage fee is typical.

chatter: Card fees are up. Look at the margin on the cheap lines.
Every sock costs a penny more to sell.

events.title: Payment outage
events.headline: Card payments down for hours across online shops
events.story: A fault at a payment processor has stopped card payments across the country. Online shops report baskets that will not complete. The fault was fixed by the evening.

why.demand.all: Customers cannot finish paying.
why.contact_rate: Customers write in to say it will not take their card.

chatter: Nobody can pay. It is not us. Say so.
Fault fixed. Send a nudge to the abandoned baskets.

events.title: Chargebacks tighten
events.headline: Banks make it easier for customers to dispute a payment
events.story: Banks have updated their rules so that a disputed payment is refunded at once. Shops are expected to see more disputes. The cost lands on the seller.

why.contact_rate: More customers ask for a refund first.
why.costs.card_fee: Dispute fees add a small cost to every sale.

chatter: More disputes. Reply fast, it matters.
A chargeback costs us more than a refund.

events.title: Minimum wage rise
events.headline: National minimum wage rises in April
events.story: The government has raised the national minimum wage. Suppliers and couriers with low-paid staff are expected to pass a small part of that on. The shop's own wage bill is up too.

why.costs.goods: Suppliers pass on a share of higher wages.

chatter: The new rate starts this month. Check the rota costs.
Suppliers have written. It is a small rise, they say.

events.title: Suppliers raise their prices
events.headline: Suppliers pass on higher costs to small shops
events.story: Several suppliers have written to say prices will rise. Materials and energy are both up. Shops are choosing between smaller margins and higher prices.

why.costs.goods: A typical rise of about three percent.

chatter: Supplier letter: three percent from next month.
Prices up on the cost side. Check the shelf prices.

events.title: Supplier prices ease
events.headline: Raw material prices ease; suppliers offer small cuts
events.story: After a long rise, the cost of several raw materials has begun to fall. Suppliers have offered small discounts to keep their larger customers. It is a modest relief.

why.costs.goods: A small discount of about three percent.

chatter: Supplier has dropped the price a little. Take it.
Margin looks better this month.

events.title: Energy price cap rises
events.headline: Energy price cap goes up in the new quarter
events.story: The regulator has raised the cap on household and business energy prices. Factories and warehouses pay more. Households are expected to tighten their spending.

why.demand.all: Households spend a little less.
why.costs.goods: Suppliers' energy costs are passed on.

chatter: Energy bill is up. So are the supplier prices.
Orders are a bit slower. It must be the bills.

events.title: Interest rates rise
events.headline: Interest rates rise again
events.story: The central bank has raised its interest rate. Mortgages and credit cards will cost more. People are tightening their budgets.

why.demand.all: Slightly tighter household budgets.

chatter: Orders slightly lighter. Mortgages, probably.
Rates are up. So is the caution.

events.title: Cost-of-living squeeze
events.headline: Households cut back as bills mount
events.story: Rising prices are squeezing family budgets. Surveys show people putting off gifts and small treats. Cheap comforts hold up best.

why.demand.all: Less spare money for gifts.
why.demand.products.trophy: A gift for no reason is the first to go.

chatter: Cancellations are up. People are being careful.
Cheap lines hold. Gifts are quieter.

events.title: Consumer confidence rises
events.headline: Shoppers feel better about their money
events.story: A closely watched survey shows consumer confidence at a two-year high. Wages have outpaced prices and people are spending. Shops report the best month in a while.

why.demand.all: People spend a little more freely.

chatter: A good month. Do not get excited.
Gift orders are up. Check stock.

events.title: Import duty on small parcels
events.headline: New duty on small imported parcels
events.story: The government has changed the duty rules on goods under a certain value. Shops that import small components now pay a little more. Customers are not expected to notice.

why.costs.goods: A small duty on imported goods.

chatter: A duty form on every box. Annoying.
Goods cost a little more; no change on the shelf yet.

events.title: Levy on sweet foods
events.headline: Government extends a levy on sweet foods
events.story: A health levy on sugary food has been widened. Biscuits and snacks are now covered. Shops selling them have a small cost increase to absorb or pass on.

why.demand.categories.food: Higher prices put some buyers off.
why.costs.goods: A small levy on supplier invoices.

chatter: The tin costs a little more to make.
Food sales are a bit softer. Might be the levy.

events.title: New packaging rule
events.headline: Packaging rules tighten for online sellers
events.story: New rules require sellers to show the recycled content of their packaging and pay a charge on the rest. Suppliers are adjusting and some boxes cost more. Shops are told to check their labels.

why.supplier_late_chance: Suppliers take time to change their boxes.

chatter: New label on every box. Print a test.
The packaging bill is up a bit.

events.title: Cotton shortage
events.headline: Cotton harvest short; mills warn of late deliveries
events.story: A poor harvest has cut the supply of cotton. Mills are rationing their output and prices are up. Sock and textile makers are warning of delays.

why.supplier_late_chance: Mills ration orders, so deliveries slip.

chatter: Socks are late from the mill. Cotton.
Supplier asked us to be patient. We are being patient.

events.title: Cardboard shortage
events.headline: Cardboard in short supply; boxes cost more
events.story: Paper mills have cut production and the price of corrugated board is up. Shops report waiting longer for boxes. Some are switching to what they can find.
chatter: Boxes are late. Packing on spare ones.
Cardboard price up. Everything we send is in a box.

events.title: Bread flour shortage
events.headline: Bakers short of flour as mills fall behind
events.story: A poor wheat harvest and a mill fault have left bakers short of flour. Bread is dearer in the shops. Anyone making sandwiches is feeling it.

why.demand.products.emergency-sandwich: A dearer sandwich sells slightly less.

chatter: Bread is short. The sandwich is the first to know.
Baker says tomorrow. They said that yesterday.

events.title: Electronics shortage
events.headline: Chip shortage hits small gadget makers
events.story: A shortage of small electronic chips has slowed the making of phones and speakers. Makers say orders will be filled in the order they came. Prices are up.

why.supplier_late_chance: Gadget makers are behind on orders.

chatter: Blip stock is late again. Not our factory.
Supplier quote went up seven percent.

events.title: Foam shortage
events.headline: Foam makers short of a key chemical
events.story: A plant fault has cut the supply of the chemical used to make soft foam. Cushion and padding makers are on allocation. Foam prices are rising.
chatter: Foam for the helmet is on allocation.
Cap lining supplier is a week behind.

events.title: Plastic film shortage
events.headline: Plastic film in short supply
events.story: A shortage of the film used for wrapping and air-cushion sheets has hit packers and manufacturers. Prices have risen. Suppliers are rationing orders.
chatter: Bubble wrap supplier is behind. Funny.
Film price up. Watch the bubble margin.

events.title: Cocoa and sugar costs spike
events.headline: Chocolate and biscuit prices rise as cocoa costs spike
events.story: Cocoa and sugar prices have risen sharply after bad harvests. Biscuit makers are raising their prices. Shops are warned to expect smaller tins.

why.costs.goods: Biscuit makers pass on the commodity price.

chatter: Tin supplier raised the price. Bad cocoa year.
Biscuits cost more to fill the tin.

events.title: A rival shop launches
events.headline: A new online shop opens selling much the same things
events.story: A new online shop has opened with a bold launch and a big advertising budget. It sells similar products at similar prices. Early customers are said to be trying both.

why.demand.all: A few customers try the new shop.

chatter: There is a new shop out there. Sells something similar.
Not a disaster. Keep the service better.

events.title: A rival closes
events.headline: Online shop closes after a difficult year
events.story: A well-known online shop selling similar goods has announced it is shutting. Its customers are looking for somewhere else. Smaller shops are reporting a lift.

why.demand.all: Orphaned customers buy here.
why.visits: More searches land on the shop.

chatter: A rival has shut. Be kind about it.
More new customers this week than usual.

events.title: A rival recalls a padded cap
events.headline: Rival recalls padded head protection over loose lining
events.story: A competing seller has recalled a padded cap after the lining came loose. Customers are checking their own. Shops that sell a well-made one are getting questions.

why.demand.products.indoor-helmet: Shoppers switch to a well-made one.
why.contact_rate: Customers check that theirs is fine.

chatter: Our lining is sewn. Say so.
Helmet questions are up. Reassure and move on.

events.title: Search ranking change (down)
events.headline: Search engine changes its ranking; small shops slip
events.story: A major search engine has updated how it ranks websites. Small online shops report falling visits. Experts say it will take weeks to settle.

why.visits: The shop moves down the results.

chatter: Traffic is down a fifth. The search engine changed something.
It will settle. It always does.

events.title: Search ranking change (up)
events.headline: Search update favours small independent shops
events.story: A search engine update has pushed small independent shops up the results. Visits have risen for sites with original writing. The effect is expected to fade.

why.visits: The shop moves up the results.

chatter: Traffic is up a fifth. Search likes our product pages.
Enjoy it. Do not rely on it.

events.title: Website hosting outage
events.headline: Hosting fault takes a swathe of online shops offline
events.story: A fault at a large web host has taken thousands of websites offline for several hours. Shops that depend on it have been unable to sell. Normal service is back.

why.demand.all: The shop cannot sell while it is offline.
why.contact_rate: Customers write in to ask what happened.

chatter: We were off the web for part of the day. Not ours.
Stuck. Wait, then tell people.

events.title: Social media outage
events.headline: Social networks go down for a day
events.story: Several social networks have been down since the morning. Shops that rely on them for traffic have seen it vanish. Posts will reappear later.
chatter: Social is down. Traffic is quieter.
No post today. Nobody would see it.

events.title: Listed on a comparison site
events.headline: Price comparison site adds small shops to its listings
events.story: A popular price comparison site has opened its listings to small shops. Shops that signed up report more visits. The site takes a small fee on each sale.

why.demand.all: A small lift in orders from the listing.

chatter: A new traffic source. Check the fee.
Comparison shoppers ask more questions.

events.title: Local radio mention
events.headline: Shop mentioned on a morning radio phone-in
events.story: A caller on a local morning phone-in described a favourite shop at length. The presenter laughed and agreed. The shop had a busy few days.

why.demand.all: Some of them buy.

chatter: Radio mention. Traffic is up.
Someone said 'I heard about you on the radio'.

events.title: A bad review travels
events.headline: One-star review shared thousands of times
events.story: A customer's unhappy review has been shared widely. The facts are disputed but the post is vivid. The shop has replied politely and is waiting for it to pass.

why.demand.all: Some shoppers are put off.
why.contact_rate: A few customers ask about the story.

chatter: A bad review is going round. Do not argue.
Reply once, politely.

events.title: A good review travels
events.headline: Five-star review shared thousands of times
events.story: A customer's delighted review has been shared widely. People are pointing to it as proof. The shop has said thank you and gone back to packing.

why.demand.all: The review nudges shoppers to buy.

chatter: A lovely review is going round.
Say thank you. Do not overdo it.

events.title: Gift guide: the sock
events.headline: Newspaper gift guide picks a single sock
events.story: A national newspaper's gift guide has included the Spare Sock as 'the gift for the person who has everything but a matching pair'. The paper's readers took it seriously. The shop saw the effect within the hour.

why.demand.products.spare-sock: It was the featured product.

chatter: The sock is in the paper. Check the stock.
Sock orders in the hundreds. Not a joke.

events.title: Gift guide: the tin
events.headline: Gift guide names a biscuit tin the best present for people you do not know well
events.story: A weekend magazine's gift guide has chosen the Biscuit Tin for people you have to buy for but cannot think of anything. Readers agreed. The tin sold out in some colours.
chatter: The tin made the guide. Reorder now.
Stock is going down by the hour.

events.title: Gift guide: the trophy
events.headline: Magazine recommends a trophy that says only 'Well done.'
events.story: A lifestyle magazine's gift guide recommends the Trophy as a present for anyone who has done something small. The writer said it was the funniest present he gave all year. Orders followed.
chatter: The trophy is in the magazine. Count the stock.
People want it for the office.

events.title: Gift guide: the pen
events.headline: Stationery column picks one good pen
events.story: A national newspaper's stationery column has named One Good Pen the sensible pick for anyone who writes more than once a week. Readers like a clear recommendation. The pen sold well.
chatter: Pen in the paper. Check the box.
It is the reviewer who said 'one is enough'. Funny.

events.title: A sock goes viral
events.headline: Video of a sock rejoining its pair watched four million times
events.story: A short film of a customer reuniting a single sock with its pair has gone round the internet. Viewers say it is oddly moving. The shop is not sure what to make of it.

why.demand.products.spare-sock: The product in the video.

chatter: The sock is trending. I cannot explain it.
Order count is a number I have not seen before.
Check supply. Do it now.

events.title: A helmet goes viral
events.headline: Man walks into low beam in viral film; wears helmet in the sequel
events.story: A film of a tall man striking his head on a low beam has been watched millions of times. A follow-up shows him wearing a padded cap. Viewers are asking where to buy one.
chatter: The helmet is the new thing. Do not ask.
Stock is tight on the helmet.

events.title: A sandwich goes viral
events.headline: Hungry commuter praises 'an emergency sandwich, delivered'
events.story: A commuter stuck at a station posted a picture of a sandwich that arrived by post at the platform. It has been shared by thousands who wish it had happened to them. The shop was surprised.
chatter: Sandwich orders are up. It is the picture.
Chilled courier is nearly full.

events.title: A puddle goes viral
events.headline: Tiny tray of water becomes a household pet
events.story: A man's film of himself looking after a puddle on a small tray has been watched endlessly. Viewers are leaving comments about how restful it is. The Starter Puddle has been sold out in two sizes.
chatter: Puddle orders. Don't ask why.
A restful film has done this.

events.title: Stones go viral
events.headline: Skimming record broken by a man in a suit
events.story: A man in a suit has broken a local skimming record on camera. The film has been watched millions of times. Skimming Stones, Graded, are the stones he used.
chatter: Stones are suddenly a thing.
Grade three is gone.

events.title: An aeroplane goes viral
events.headline: Paper aeroplane thrown from a tower lands at the other end of town
events.story: A paper aeroplane thrown from a roof has been tracked across a whole town by an enthusiastic crowd. A video has been shared widely. The shop's aeroplane is the one in the film.
chatter: The aeroplane flew a long way. So have the orders.
Everyone wants to throw one off a roof. Do not encourage it.

events.title: Bubble wrap goes viral
events.headline: Satisfying film of already-popped bubble wrap gets millions of views
events.story: A film in which a woman slowly unrolls pre-popped bubble wrap in complete silence has been watched millions of times. Viewers say it is calming. The shop shipped hundreds of rolls in a week.
chatter: The silent bubble wrap film has done it.
Packers are working on a Sunday.

events.title: An umbrella goes viral
events.headline: Woman defends the Other Umbrella in a storm, on camera
events.story: A film shows a woman keeping dry in a gale under the Other Umbrella while all around her fail. The clip has been shared by weather presenters. Orders came in all night.
chatter: The umbrella is a hero. Do not tell it.
A weather presenter held it up.

events.title: A jungle goes viral
events.headline: A pocket-sized forest becomes this month's favourite desk object
events.story: A designer showed off a desk with the Pocket Jungle and it went round the internet in a day. Viewers say it makes an office look intentional. The shop is reordering.
chatter: Pocket Jungle is on the desk of a thousand strangers.
Reorder the jungle.

events.title: Decluttering trend
events.headline: A nation tidies its drawers and buys fewer things
events.story: A craze for decluttering has swept the country, with films of cupboards being emptied. People are buying packing and storage but few new objects. Small useful items fare best.

why.demand.all: People hold back on new buying.
why.demand.products.one-good-pen: One good pen replaces the drawer of dead ones.

chatter: More 'sending things back' than usual.
Everyone is clearing out a drawer.

events.title: Working from home wave
events.headline: More firms let staff work from home
events.story: Several large employers have told staff they may work from home most days. Home offices are being kitted out. Desk goods are in demand and lunch deliveries fall.

why.demand.products.one-good-pen: A decent pen for the home desk.
why.demand.products.starter-puddle: Something to look at on a video call.
why.demand.products.emergency-sandwich: Fewer people stuck at their desk without lunch.
why.demand.categories.desk-home: People kit out the spare room.

chatter: Desk things are doing well. Home offices.
More daytime browsing than usual.

events.title: Picnic craze
events.headline: A national mania for picnics
events.story: Parks are full of blankets and baskets. Picnic food and outdoor goods are in demand. The shops are not complaining.

why.demand.products.skimming-stones: Something to do at the lake.

chatter: Sandwiches are flying. Picnic season.
Daypacks are moving.

events.title: Houseplant boom
events.headline: Houseplants are the new essential
events.story: Garden centres report queues for leafy plants and online shops report the same. Small desk plants are the easiest to buy. The Pocket Jungle has been on several lists.

why.demand.products.pocket-jungle: People want a plant that is easy to keep.

chatter: Plants are in. The Pocket Jungle is selling.
People ask if it needs water. It does not.

events.title: Walking craze
events.headline: The nation takes a long walk
events.story: A rise in country walking has been recorded across the whole of Britain. Maps and bags are out of stock. The shop's daypack is among the favourites.

why.demand.products.other-umbrella: Weather is optional; an umbrella is not.

chatter: Walkers are buying packs.
Somebody wrote 'for the Pennine Way'. That is not a pack.

events.title: Retro audio revival
events.headline: The speaker you can hold is back
events.story: A taste for compact, old-style music players has come back among younger listeners. Boomboxes are on the lists. Small gadgets with a button are doing well.

why.demand.products.boombox-mini: A small boombox suits the fashion.
why.demand.products.blip: A very small phone is part of the same taste.

chatter: The Boombox Mini is on a playlist of 'retro things'.
Small gadgets are in.

events.title: Corporate thank-you wave
events.headline: Firms send staff small thank-you gifts
events.story: Several large employers have announced they will send each member of staff a small thank-you gift. Smaller firms are following. Gift orders from businesses rose sharply.

why.demand.all: A general lift from bulk buyers.

chatter: Business orders for twenty at a time. Good.
Bulk invoices going out.

events.title: The Wolf blows down two houses
events.headline: Wolf blows down two houses in Pigs' Lane; third stands firm
events.story: A wolf reporting a bad cold has blown down two houses in Pigs' Lane, one of straw and one of sticks. The occupants are unhurt and now sleeping at the brick house at the end. Insurers say they will attend when the roof is back on. Residents are asking where they can buy sturdier things.
events.source: The Three Little Pigs, traditional English folk tale

why.demand.products.indoor-helmet: Falling bricks and rafters make a padded cap sensible.
why.contact_rate: Residents ask about delivery to a temporary address.
why.carrier_delay_days: Couriers cannot find the new address.
why.reach: Everyone reads about the Pigs' Lane houses in the paper; a few people far from the lane buy a padded cap too.

chatter: Pigs' Lane needs helmets. All of them.
Three change-of-address emails from the same family.
The brick house has no spare room for deliveries.

events.title: Humpty Dumpty has a great fall
events.headline: Humpty Dumpty falls from wall; the king's men unable to help
events.story: A large, egg-shaped gentleman fell from a wall this morning and has not been put together again. The king's horses and men attended but could not help. Several residents have since been seen near walls wearing padded caps.

why.demand.products.indoor-helmet: A padded cap is the obvious lesson.
why.visits: News spreads and shoppers look up head protection.

chatter: Humpty has fallen. Helmet orders are up.
Someone wrote 'to avoid being a Humpty'.
We do not do egg care.

events.title: Jack and Jill tumble
events.headline: Two residents tumble down a hill with a pail of water
events.story: Jack and Jill climbed a hill to fetch a pail of water and came down faster than they went up. Jack has broken his crown and Jill is said to have followed. Neighbours are asking about protective headwear and a better pail.

why.demand.products.indoor-helmet: A broken crown makes the case for a padded cap.
why.demand.products.starter-puddle: A tidy tray is easier than a pail.
why.reach: The tumble makes the national pages; a few parents elsewhere buy a padded cap.

chatter: Jack and Jill again. Helmets.
They want something for the water too.
Sign the get-well card.

events.title: A beanstalk blocks the road
events.headline: Giant beanstalk blocks road to market
events.story: A beanstalk of unknown origin rose overnight on the road to market and now stands above the church. The council has put cones round it. Couriers report that nothing will pass until it has been felled.
events.source: Jack and the Beanstalk, traditional English folk tale

why.demand.all: Fewer shoppers can leave the lane.
why.carrier_delay_days: No courier gets past the stalk.

chatter: Beanstalk. Deliveries held.
A neighbour has asked if the Pocket Jungle will grow that large.
It will not.

events.title: Porridge and a broken chair
events.headline: Three bears report porridge eaten and chair broken
events.story: A family of bears has reported a break-in at their cottage in the wood. Three bowls of porridge were disturbed, one chair broken and one bed slept in. They are replacing their furniture and shopping for provisions.
events.source: Goldilocks and the Three Bears, English folk tale (Southey, 1837)

why.demand.all: A household re-stocking in the wood.
why.demand.products.emergency-sandwich: The bears need something quick while they tidy.

chatter: Three of everything again, said the bears.
They would like a tin that is just right.
Our tins come in one size.

events.title: A basket for Grandmother
events.headline: Girl's basket delivery to grandmother goes wrong
events.story: A young woman in a red hood took a basket of cakes and wine to her grandmother and had a conversation with an animal on the way. All parties are safe but the basket was late. Local delivery services are now being asked to be punctual and, where possible, wolf-proof.
events.source: Little Red Riding Hood, Perrault and the Brothers Grimm

why.demand.products.biscuit-tin: Cakes for relatives, now in tins.

chatter: A basket is not a daypack. We have said so.
Cakes for Grandmother. Tin.
Someone asked if we deliver to the wood. We do.

events.title: A house made of sweets
events.headline: Council investigates a house made of confectionery
events.story: Planners are looking into a cottage in the forest built of bread, cake and sugar. The owner says the house is for the sake of visitors. Two children are reported to have found it very agreeable and then less so.

why.demand.products.biscuit-tin: Sweet buyers inspired by the cottage.
why.demand.products.paper-aeroplane: A trail of crumbs and paper.

chatter: Everyone wants a house made of biscuits.
Do not follow breadcrumbs. Say it.
Tin orders are up.

events.title: Delivery to a tower
events.headline: Tower resident asks couriers to climb a rope of hair
events.story: A resident of a tall tower with no door has asked couriers to deliver by rope. The rope, it transpires, is a person's hair. Couriers have declined, citing safety. Parcels are being left at the foot of the tower.

why.contact_rate: The customer asks how to receive a parcel.
why.carrier_delay_days: Parcels sit at the tower base until someone can climb.

chatter: She wants it delivered to the top. We cannot.
A safe place, said the courier. No.
Write it on the delivery note: ground floor.

events.title: The Royal Ball
events.headline: Royal ball announced for Saturday; guests must leave by midnight
events.story: The king has invited every eligible young woman to a ball on Saturday. Guests have been asked to leave by midnight, which a spokesman said was a firm rule. Shoes, gloves and last-minute gifts are selling briskly.

why.demand.all: Guests buy gifts and accessories.
why.demand.products.spare-sock: One lost shoe means a spare is useful.
why.demand.products.trophy: A gift for whoever wins the evening.
why.reach: The lost slipper is in every paper; odd-sock buying picks up a little everywhere.

chatter: Midnight is a rule. Everyone keeps asking.
Spare sock. Of course.
We do not make shoes.

events.title: The Piper leaves town
events.headline: Piper leaves Hamelin after dispute over his fee
events.story: A piper who cleared the town of rats has left with the town's children after a dispute over his fee. The council has not commented. School supplies in the town are untouched and stationery sales have fallen.
events.source: The Pied Piper of Hamelin, Robert Browning (1842), after a German legend
chatter: The usual schools do not seem to be ordering.
Do not ask about the fee.
No children. Fewer aeroplanes.

events.title: A man wakes after twenty years
events.headline: Man wakes after twenty-year sleep; asks about an old order
events.story: A man in worn clothes has walked into the village with a beard to his waist and asked about an order he placed twenty years ago. The village records office is checking. The man says he has a good excuse.

why.contact_rate: A twenty-year-old order is an unusual question.

chatter: An order from twenty years ago. Check the archive.
He is polite and quite confused.
We do not have a record. We were not here.

events.title: The castle wakes
events.headline: Castle wakes after a hundred years; household wants everything
events.story: A castle that has slept for a hundred years has woken, and the household is making up for lost time. Orders for everyday goods arrived in the first hour. The household asks that its hundred-year-old account be reopened.
events.source: Sleeping Beauty, Charles Perrault (1697) and the Brothers Grimm

why.demand.all: A whole castle needs restocking.
why.demand.products.spare-sock: A hundred years without fresh socks.

chatter: The castle is back. Big order incoming.
A hundred years of dust, said the footman.
They would like it all before dinner.

events.title: Warning on accepting food at the door
events.headline: Residents told not to accept apples from strangers
events.story: A local advisory asks residents not to accept food from strangers at the door. An apple seller is said to be involved. Households are being more careful about where their food comes from.

why.demand.products.emergency-sandwich: Fewer people buying food from sellers they do not know.
why.contact_rate: Customers ask where food is made.

chatter: Customers want to know where the tin was made.
Our food is from a bakery with a name.
Do not offer anyone an apple.

events.title: A name must be guessed
events.headline: Couriers refuse to deliver until a customer's name is guessed
events.story: A customer in the forest has told the courier that the parcel may be handed over only if the name on the label is guessed correctly. Couriers have said they have a rota for that. Both parties are said to be patient.

why.contact_rate: Customers ask us to confirm the name on the label.
why.carrier_delay_days: Parcels held until a name is agreed.

chatter: Please confirm the name on the parcel.
Is it Tom? Is it Dick? No.
A good label saves an hour.

events.title: Overnight production by unknown hands
events.headline: Small night workers keep a shoemaker in business
events.story: A shoemaker has reported that his orders are being filled each night by two small workers nobody has seen. He has not asked questions. Other makers say they would also like a few small workers.
events.source: The Elves and the Shoemaker, Brothers Grimm

why.supplier_late_chance: Orders arrive on time because the night shift works.
why.costs.goods: A supplier cutting costs passes a little on.

chatter: Supplier is early. No one asked why.
The goods arrive a day ahead. Do not question it.
Leave out a bowl of milk.

events.title: A procession of the new clothes
events.headline: Emperor processes in new clothes; a child objects
events.story: The emperor walked in procession through the city in clothes that nobody else could see. A child observed that he wore nothing at all. Tailors report a sudden interest in plain items that actually exist.
events.source: The Emperor's New Clothes, Hans Christian Andersen (1837)

why.demand.all: A small lift from curiosity.
why.demand.products.spare-sock: At least a sock is a sock.
why.contact_rate: Questions about whether goods are real.

chatter: Customers keep asking if the sock is a real sock. It is.
It is on the page. Look.
Nothing here is invisible.

events.title: The bed with twenty mattresses
events.headline: Household stacks twenty mattresses to test a single pea
events.story: A royal household has placed twenty mattresses and as many eiderdowns on one bed over a single pea. A guest has said she slept poorly. The household is shopping for padding.
events.source: The Princess and the Pea, Hans Christian Andersen (1835)
chatter: The pea test needs wrap, apparently.
Bubble wrap on a pea. Thorough.
Do not ask which came first.

events.title: A golden ball lost in a well
events.headline: Princess's golden ball lost down a well; frog offers help
events.story: A royal golden ball has fallen into a well and a frog has offered to get it back for a price. The king has taken an interest. Households in the area are putting their own golden objects out of reach.

why.demand.products.trophy: A shiny gold object is a comfort.

chatter: Do not put a trophy near a well.
A frog may be a prince. We do not know.
Gold things are selling.

events.title: The Gingerbread Man runs off
events.headline: Gingerbread man escapes oven and runs across the county
events.story: A newly baked gingerbread man has left an oven and is running across the countryside. He cannot be caught, he says. Couriers have not been able to deliver to him either.
events.source: The Gingerbread Man, traditional English folk tale

why.demand.products.biscuit-tin: Everyone wants to be near a gingerbread man.
why.carrier_delay_days: The customer will not sit still.

chatter: Run, run, as fast as you can. And so do the couriers.
Tin orders rose. Gingerbread.
No, we cannot catch him.

events.title: The sky is falling
events.headline: Hen reports falling sky; acorn found at scene
events.story: A hen reports that a piece of the sky has fallen on her head. An acorn was recovered at the scene. The affected residents are advising each other to wear something sensible and visit the king.

why.demand.products.indoor-helmet: A padded cap is a reasonable reply to a falling sky.
why.contact_rate: Questions about whether it is serious.
why.reach: The sky story is all over the news, so some people everywhere decide a helmet is sensible.

chatter: The sky is not falling. Helmets are, still.
An acorn is not weather.
Everybody has panicked.

events.title: The crowded shoe
events.headline: Householder in a shoe struggles to feed many children
events.story: A woman living in a large shoe has said she has so many children she does not know what to do. She has been giving them broth without bread. Bread and socks are in short supply in the shoe.
events.source: Traditional nursery rhyme (Old Woman Who Lived in a Shoe)

why.demand.products.spare-sock: A great many feet in a small shoe.

chatter: The shoe wants forty socks.
Bread for the shoe, please.
Bulk discount is not a thing.

events.title: Cupboard bare
events.headline: Lady finds cupboard bare; dog goes without
events.story: A lady has gone to the cupboard to fetch her dog a bone and found it empty. The dog has not commented. Shops in the lane report a rush on anything that can be eaten at once.

why.demand.products.biscuit-tin: A tin, to keep a cupboard full.

chatter: Cupboard bare. Sandwiches.
The dog gets a biscuit.
Eight orders in an hour. Same lane.

events.title: The missing flock
events.headline: Shepherdess loses her sheep, advised to leave them alone
events.story: A young shepherdess reports that her sheep have wandered off and she does not know where to find them. Neighbours advise that they will come home on their own, tails behind them. A search party has packed lunches anyway.

why.demand.products.emergency-sandwich: A packed lunch for the search.

chatter: Search party. Daypacks.
They will come home on their own.
Lunch for twenty, please.

events.title: A merry old soul calls for music
events.headline: King calls for pipe, bowl and three fiddlers
events.story: The king, said to be a merry old soul, has called for his pipe, his bowl and his three fiddlers. The fiddlers have not turned up. Portable music players are being ordered in their place.

why.demand.products.boombox-mini: A boombox in place of three fiddlers.

chatter: The king would like music. Order the boombox.
He did not ask for volume.
Three fiddlers is a lot.

events.title: The clock strikes one
events.headline: Mouse runs up clock; local time declared unreliable
events.story: A mouse ran up the clock in the lane and the clock struck one. Residents say they do not trust it any more. Several are unsure what time the order cut-off falls.

why.visits: Late-night browsing while they wait for the clock.
why.contact_rate: Customers ask what time the cut-off is.

chatter: Cut-off is at six, on any clock.
The mouse has not been seen since.
Customers are asking whether the clock is wrong.

events.title: A lamb at school
events.headline: Lamb follows girl to school; teacher unamused
events.story: A small lamb followed a girl to school and was removed by the teacher. The girl's classmates found it very funny. Stationery and school items are selling briskly.
events.source: Mary Had a Little Lamb, Sarah Josepha Hale (1830)

why.demand.products.one-good-pen: A pen for a child who may now stay.

chatter: School items in the lane. The lamb.
It is not allowed in class. Obviously.
Ordered a pen for the teacher.

events.title: Spider interrupts curds and whey
events.headline: Spider sits down beside young lady at her tuffet
events.story: A young lady eating curds and whey on a tuffet was frightened away when a spider sat down beside her. The spider has since left. Residents are wary of anything with legs.

why.demand.products.emergency-sandwich: A sandwich is a safer lunch than curds.

chatter: Not a spider. It is a pocket jungle.
Curds and whey are not in stock.
Fewer plants this week. Reasons obvious.

events.title: A candlestick contest
events.headline: Jack leaps candlestick, wins local contest
events.story: Jack, who is nimble and quick, has leapt over a candlestick for the third time this week. A trophy was awarded and a helmet recommended. Spectators have been told not to try it at home.
chatter: Do not try this at home. Helmets, though.
Trophy for Jack. 'Well done.'
Candle safety not our department.

events.title: The great race
events.headline: Tortoise beats hare in long-distance race
events.story: A tortoise has beaten a hare in a race across the meadow after the hare took a nap. The tortoise says it kept going. A trophy was presented and a lesson is said to have been learned.
events.source: The Tortoise and the Hare, Aesop

why.carrier_delay_days: A hare's courier is not one to hurry.

chatter: Slow and steady has won. Trophy time.
The hare has asked for a refund.
The tortoise would like to be paid in lettuce.

events.title: The boy who cried wolf
events.headline: Villagers ignore a shepherd boy's alarm; wolf is real
events.story: A shepherd boy's repeated false alarms have made the villagers slow to react. This week the wolf was real. The village is reviewing how it handles alerts.
events.source: The Boy Who Cried Wolf, Aesop

why.contact_rate: Customers are unsure if a delivery alert is real.

chatter: Is this delivery text real? Check the sender.
Alerts only for real things.
The shop does not cry wolf.

events.title: The ant stocks for winter
events.headline: Ant stocks up for winter while grasshopper sings
events.story: An ant has ordered a winter's supplies while a grasshopper has played the fiddle all summer. The grasshopper has been seen asking for credit. The shop reports orders from the meadow that look unusually thorough.
events.source: The Ant and the Grasshopper, Aesop

why.demand.all: Large, careful orders from the meadow.

chatter: Big list from the meadow. All neat.
The grasshopper wants credit. No.
The ant paid on time.

events.title: Sour grapes review
events.headline: Fox declares grapes sour after failing to reach them
events.story: A fox has posted a one-star review of a vineyard after failing to reach the grapes. He says they were probably sour. Other shops have noted that a bad review from someone who never bought anything is still a bad review.
events.source: The Fox and the Grapes, Aesop

why.demand.all: A small drop in confidence.
why.contact_rate: A few questions about the story.

chatter: A review from someone who did not buy.
Reply once. Politely.
He has a fan club, apparently.

events.title: A wooden boy goes to school
events.headline: Wooden boy sells his schoolbook for a ticket
events.story: A wooden boy sent to school sold his book to buy a ticket to a puppet show. His father has since had to buy a replacement and a new pen. The boy says his nose grows when he is untruthful, which is a lot.
events.source: The Adventures of Pinocchio, Carlo Collodi (1883)
chatter: His father ordered another pen.
Nose grows when untruthful. Ours does not.
Pinocchio wants a refund. His father says no.

events.title: A cat in boots makes a gift
events.headline: Cat in boots delivers rabbits to king on master's behalf
events.story: A cat wearing boots has delivered a succession of rabbits and partridges to the king on behalf of his master. The king is said to be impressed. Boot liners and gifts are selling briskly.

why.demand.all: A fashion for impressing royalty.
why.demand.products.spare-sock: A sock goes inside a boot.

chatter: A cat in boots. The sock is a match.
Gifts for the king are in.
We do not make boots.

events.title: Seven small miners take a long break
events.headline: Seven miners down tools after a visitor moves in
events.story: Seven small miners have stopped work after a visitor moved into their cottage. Their mine supplies metals to several makers. Deliveries have slowed and the miners have said they will be back when they have sung a few more songs.

why.supplier_late_chance: A mine on a break means late goods.
why.costs.goods: A small increase while supply is short.

chatter: The mine is on a break. Supplier says whistle later.
Metal parts are late.
They are very small. They are also quite firm.

events.title: Four animals form a band
events.headline: Four animals set out for Bremen to be town musicians
events.story: A donkey, a dog, a cat and a rooster have formed a band and are travelling to Bremen. They have been heard from a long way off. Passers-by say they are better than they sound.
events.source: The Town Musicians of Bremen, Brothers Grimm
chatter: A band of four. Boombox demand up.
Noise complaints have started.
They are better than they sound.

events.title: A pea-soup fog
events.headline: Thick fog settles on London; parcels a day late
events.story: A yellow fog has settled over the city and shows no sign of lifting. Cabmen are walking beside their horses and the couriers are doing the same. A parcel that should arrive in the morning is expected in the afternoon of the following day.
events.source: Bleak House, Charles Dickens (1853); the Sherlock Holmes stories, Arthur Conan Doyle

why.contact_rate: Customers ask where their parcel is.
why.carrier_delay_days: Drivers cannot see; parcels run a day late.

chatter: The fog is down. Parcels move at the speed of a man with a lantern.
A courier has said he will deliver by morning, by which he means Thursday.
Tell them kindly. It is the weather.

events.title: A wager on a world tour
events.headline: Gentleman wagers he can circle the world in eighty days; delivery promises scrutinised
events.story: A gentleman at his club has staked half his fortune that he can go round the world in eighty days. Newspapers are now checking every delivery promise in the land against the calendar. Shops are being asked, firmly, what they mean by 'two days'.
events.source: Around the World in Eighty Days, Jules Verne (1872)

why.visits: Curious shoppers look up delivery times.
why.contact_rate: Customers ask whether the promised date is exact.

chatter: Customers want the date to be exact. It is as exact as the post.
Do not promise 'within eighty days'.
Check the delivery wording on every page.

events.title: Mr Toad crashes another motor-car
events.headline: Motor-car found in a ditch; owner says he was only just starting
events.story: A motor-car has been recovered from a ditch near the river. Its owner, an enthusiastic and frequently unlucky amphibian, says he was only just starting. He has ordered more goggles and a great deal of padding.
events.source: The Wind in the Willows, Kenneth Grahame (1908)

why.reach: Mr Toad's crash is reported widely and sets people thinking about bumps and bubble wrap.

chatter: Toad again. Helmet reorder.
He has asked for a motoring helmet. We do not do those.
He will not listen to the sensible ones.

events.title: The Riverbank floods
events.headline: River bursts its banks; riverside residents sleep upstairs
events.story: The river has risen after a week of rain and entered several riverside homes. Residents are living on the upper floors and visiting each other by boat. Couriers cannot reach the lower road.
events.source: The Wind in the Willows, Kenneth Grahame (1908)

why.demand.all: People are busy moving furniture.
why.demand.categories.desk-home: People stuck indoors buy for the house.
why.carrier_delay_days: Roads under water.

chatter: Delivery by boat is not a service we offer.
Riverbank is flooded. Hold the parcels.
A mole wrote to say thanks for the patience.

events.title: The tea party over-orders
events.headline: Tea party that never ends places another large order
events.story: A tea party in Wonderland, which has been in progress for some time, has placed another very large order. The hosts say it is always six o'clock and there is always room for more. Suppliers have asked for payment in advance.
events.source: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, Lewis Carroll (1865)

why.demand.all: A big order lifts the lane.
why.demand.products.biscuit-tin: A party that never ends needs tins.
why.reach: Pictures of the endless tea party travel; tea-time biscuits sell a little everywhere.

chatter: Another tea party order. Same as the last, plus a dormouse.
It is always six o'clock. We are on time.
They said no room. Then they ordered forty.

events.title: The Queen's new edicts
events.headline: Queen of Hearts issues sixteen edicts on parcels
events.story: The Queen has issued sixteen edicts on the handling of parcels, the first of which is 'off with their heads'. Couriers are checking each carefully. Deliveries are slowed while the edicts are read.
events.source: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, Lewis Carroll (1865)

why.demand.all: Some shoppers wait until it clears.
why.contact_rate: Customers ask what the new rules mean.
why.carrier_delay_days: Couriers stop to read the rules.

chatter: Sixteen new rules. Do not read the first.
The courier has asked for a lawyer.
Put the tarts in a tin.

events.title: Sizes in Wonderland
events.headline: Visitor grows and shrinks; sizing disputes follow
events.story: A young visitor has been changing size throughout the week and has asked several shops to exchange everything she bought. Returns have risen across the district. Shops say size is a state of mind.
events.source: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, Lewis Carroll (1865)

why.demand.products.daypack: People hold off on bags until they know their size.
why.demand.products.spare-sock: One size fits a lot of sizes.

chatter: She asked for a smaller one, then a larger one.
Keep the exchange rules simple.
The sock is a one-size-fits-all. It has been tested.

events.title: Pandora opens a box
events.headline: Pandora opens a box she was told to leave shut
events.story: A woman in the city has opened a box that she was told to leave shut and released a great many troubles. The neighbours are returning everything they bought that week. Shops report a rise in returns and a reluctance to open anything.
events.source: Greek myth (Pandora's box), retold by Hesiod

why.demand.all: Fewer people buy this week.

chatter: Returns have doubled. Pandora's fault.
Nobody opens a box this week.
Hope is still in the bottom, apparently.

events.title: A king turns things to gold
events.headline: King turns breakfast, daughter and trophy to gold
events.story: A king who asked for everything he touched to turn to gold has found the wish more trouble than it was worth. The trophy shop in town has seen a rush of orders for anything gold and heavy. The kitchen has had to refuse him a sandwich.
events.source: King Midas, Greek myth, retold by Ovid

why.demand.products.trophy: A gold-coloured object is now unusually popular.
why.demand.products.biscuit-tin: A tin that stays a tin.

chatter: Gold touch, everyone wants a trophy.
He tried to order a sandwich. It turned into a sandwich-shaped ingot.
Please deliver nothing to his hands.

events.title: A young flyer falls
events.headline: Young man flies too near the sun; wings fail
events.story: A young man on a pair of wax-and-feather wings flew near the sun and came down faster than he went up. He has been found alive and sheepish. Residents of Crete are being advised to stay low.
events.source: Icarus, Greek myth, retold by Ovid

why.demand.products.indoor-helmet: A padded cap is a sensible reply to a fall.

chatter: Fly low, said his father. He did not.
Paper aeroplanes are the sensible form of flight.
Helmets, again.

events.title: A large wooden gift
events.headline: Large wooden gift left at city gates; guards debate
events.story: A large wooden horse has been left at the city gates with no note. The guards have decided to bring it in. The shop has been asked to supply a great deal of padding and a very large box.
events.source: The Trojan Horse, Greek myth, retold by Virgil

why.demand.all: A busy week in the city.

chatter: Never accept a parcel you did not order.
Bubble wrap for a horse.
A very large order, sent to a very strange address.

events.title: Ten years late
events.headline: King returns from a ten-year voyage; deliveries to his island have lagged
events.story: A king has returned from a voyage that took ten years instead of one. Parcels addressed to his household have also taken a while. Island couriers say they have always been like that.

why.carrier_delay_days: Island couriers are not quick.

chatter: Tracking says 'on a ship'. For ten years.
No, we have not lost it. It is at sea.
The courier met a few monsters.

events.title: The same boulder, again
events.headline: Customer returns the same boulder for the ninth time
events.story: A resident has returned the same boulder to the shop every morning for several weeks. The shop has refunded it each time. The boulder is always back by evening.
chatter: The boulder is back. Refund processed.
We cannot say no. It is within the thirty days.
Do not look at the ledger.

events.title: Winter arrives early
events.headline: Goddess of the harvest declares winter early after daughter's departure
events.story: The goddess of the harvest has announced that autumn will begin early because her daughter has gone below. Fields are bare and the weather is cold. Households are staying indoors.
events.source: Demeter and Persephone, Greek myth (Homeric Hymn)

why.demand.all: Anxious households spend less.
why.demand.categories.food: A bad harvest means dearer food.

chatter: Early winter. Quieter on the food side.
Desk things are picking up.
The goddess is cross. Fine.

events.title: A hammer goes missing
events.headline: God's hammer stolen; thunder falls silent
events.story: The god of thunder has discovered that his hammer has been stolen by a giant who wants a bride in return. Storms have grown erratic. Deliveries are held up by strange weather.
events.source: The Lay of Thrym, Norse mythology (Poetic Edda)

why.carrier_delay_days: Erratic weather slows the rounds.

The weather has gone strange. Parcels slow.
A dress for the wedding. We do not do those either.

events.title: A sword in a stone
events.headline: Sword found in stone; every man in the realm tries to pull it
events.story: A sword has been found in a stone in the churchyard and an inscription says whoever pulls it free is king. Every man in the district has tried. A trophy has been put up for the best attempt.
events.source: Le Morte d'Arthur, Sir Thomas Malory (1485)

why.demand.products.trophy: A prize for the best attempt.

chatter: Everyone has tried to pull it. We sold a trophy.

events.title: The Round Table meets
events.headline: Round Table meets for a conference on seating
events.story: A round table has been set up for the knights of the realm to meet. The agenda has been drawn up with great care and everyone is equal. The court's stationers are busy.
events.source: Le Morte d'Arthur, Sir Thomas Malory (1485)

why.demand.all: A busy court buys supplies.
why.demand.products.one-good-pen: Someone has to take the minutes.

Nobody has a head of the table.
Twelve invoices, all equal.

events.title: A New Year's game
events.headline: Green stranger proposes beheading game at court
events.story: A green stranger rode into the court on New Year's Day and proposed a game in which one party strikes the other with an axe. Households are advised to find a sensible form of head protection. The court has been unusually quiet since.
events.source: Sir Gawain and the Green Knight, anonymous medieval poem

why.demand.products.indoor-helmet: A padded cap seems the least one can do.

chatter: A game with an axe. Helmet orders up.
