Gawain has ordered one in green.

events.title: An archery contest
events.headline: Sheriff holds archery contest; golden arrow offered
events.story: The sheriff has announced an archery contest with a golden arrow as the prize. A mysterious yeoman is said to have entered in disguise. The shops in town are busy.

why.demand.all: Spectators spend.

chatter: The contest is coming. Trophies are moving.
A yeoman in disguise placed an order.

events.title: The village cricket match
events.headline: All-day cricket match followed by a large cold lunch
events.story: The village has held a cricket match against a rival town. It lasted all day and ended with a large cold lunch. A trophy was presented and a number of hats were lost.

why.demand.products.emergency-sandwich: A cold lunch for a hundred.
why.demand.products.spare-sock: The match was muddy.

chatter: Cricket day. Sandwiches by the hundred.
Mr Pickwick would like a trophy.
A hat is not our department.

events.title: A miser's change of heart
events.headline: Notorious miser orders gifts for an entire family and a turkey
events.story: A miser known across the city for his meanness woke on Christmas morning and began buying gifts for a whole household. He sent a boy to fetch the largest turkey in the shop window. The city's tradesmen are cautiously pleased.

why.demand.all: A general rush of goodwill in the city.
why.demand.products.biscuit-tin: A gift for the whole family.
why.demand.products.spare-sock: A sock for each child.
why.demand.products.trophy: A prize for the one who kept faith.

God bless us, every one.

events.title: A boy asks for more
events.headline: Boy asks for more gruel; board is shocked
events.story: A boy at the workhouse has asked for a second helping of gruel. The board was shocked and the matter has been referred upwards. Local people, outraged, have been sending food.

Donations in kind, mostly sandwiches.
He did not ask for much.

events.title: All the clocks stopped
events.headline: Lady stops every clock at twenty to nine; time declared a private matter
events.story: A lady has stopped every clock in her house at twenty to nine and says it is now a private matter. Deliveries to the house are sent at no particular time. Her order history is long and her wedding cake is old.

why.demand.all: Little buying while time is stopped.
why.contact_rate: The household cannot say when it will be home.

No cake, thanks.

events.title: A detective is baffled by parcels
events.headline: Consulting detective receives a series of anonymous parcels
events.story: A consulting detective in Baker Street has received a series of anonymous parcels, none containing a note. Couriers have been asked for statements. He has declined to say what he thinks, which is unusual.
events.source: Sherlock Holmes stories, Arthur Conan Doyle (published before 1927)

why.carrier_delay_days: Couriers stop to give statements.

Elementary. Not our parcel.

events.title: Fifty boxes of earth
events.headline: Fifty boxes of earth shipped to a seaside town
events.story: A shipment of fifty boxes of earth has arrived at the harbour in a ship with no crew. The consignee has requested that all deliveries be made at night. Couriers have asked for double pay.

why.carrier_delay_days: Night-only deliveries.

Boxes of earth. Wrap them.
He declines invitations to garlic-free offices.

events.title: A traveller from the future
events.headline: Traveller returns from the future; orders arrive before they are placed
events.story: A traveller who has returned from the year eight hundred and two thousand has placed an order that arrived before it was made. The shop's records are puzzled. He says it will all make sense next week.
events.source: The Time Machine, H. G. Wells (1895)
chatter: The order is older than the order.
Next week, he says. We will see.
The shop has no comment on the future.

events.title: Nobody at home
events.headline: Mysterious bandaged lodger stops answering the door
events.story: A bandaged lodger at the village inn has stopped answering the door. Parcels delivered to him are being signed for by nobody. Couriers say they cannot find the recipient and have left cards.
events.source: The Invisible Man, H. G. Wells (1897)

why.carrier_delay_days: Failed delivery attempts.

chatter: Nobody home. Again.

Leave a card. He will find it.

events.title: A map in a sea-chest
events.headline: Old sea-chest yields map marked with an X
events.story: A map found in a sea-chest at the inn shows an island and a spot marked with an X. Half the district has already begun packing. The inn is asking for provisions and shovels.

why.demand.all: A rush of excited orders.

chatter: X marks the spot. Daypacks are moving.
A parrot has asked for a refund.
We do not make shovels.

events.title: The monsoon breaks
events.headline: Monsoon floods the jungle; wolves seek high ground
events.story: The monsoon has broken over the jungle and the river has overflowed. The wolf pack has moved to high ground. Residents are asking about umbrellas and whether a smaller jungle might be easier to manage.

why.demand.products.pocket-jungle: They already have more jungle than they need.
why.carrier_delay_days: Tracks and roads under water.

chatter: The jungle is wet. Everyone wants an umbrella.
No more jungle, said the order.

events.title: A cyclone lifts a house
events.headline: Cyclone lifts a farmhouse and sets it down in a strange land
events.story: A cyclone has lifted a farmhouse and set it down some way off. No one was hurt, though the house has landed on something. Deliveries to the city are delayed while the roads are cleared.
events.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz, L. Frank Baum (1900)

why.contact_rate: Customers ask where their parcel is.
why.carrier_delay_days: Roads blocked and houses in the way.

chatter: A house fell on the courier's route.
There is no place like the old address.
Slippers are not our department.

events.title: A knight charges at windmills
events.headline: Gentleman in armour charges windmills; windmills win
events.story: A gentleman in rusty armour has charged at a line of windmills, believing them to be giants. The windmills are undamaged. He has ordered a new helmet and a more sensible horse.

why.demand.products.indoor-helmet: A padded cap, for the next time.

chatter: Windmills are not giants. Helmet reorder.

events.title: A lamp is rubbed
events.headline: Street boy rubs a lamp and is granted three wishes
events.story: A street boy has rubbed an old lamp and been granted three wishes. The first was a palace; the others are under discussion. The city's shops have had their best week in years.
events.source: Aladdin, from the Arabian Nights (1001 Nights)

why.demand.all: A newly rich household spends.

chatter: A palace's worth of orders. Check stock.

Wishes are not in our contract.

events.title: Open sesame
events.headline: Forty thieves change the password on their cave
events.story: The forty thieves have changed the password on their cave and not told the thieves. Residents of the city have received an unexpected number of password reset emails. They are writing to shops asking what their own passwords were.
events.source: Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves, from the Arabian Nights

why.contact_rate: A wave of password and account questions.

chatter: Open Sesame is not a valid password.

Forty resets in an hour.

events.title: Pilgrims on the road
events.headline: Party of pilgrims sets out for the shrine; lunch ordered
events.story: A party of pilgrims has gathered at the inn and set off for the shrine, each telling a story along the way. The innkeeper has ordered lunch for all of them. Bags and sandwiches are selling.

why.demand.all: A busy inn.
why.demand.products.emergency-sandwich: A long road needs a lunch.

chatter: Pilgrims have ordered twenty-nine lunches.
The innkeeper expects a prize for the best story.
It is a long road. Bring a daypack.

events.title: Noise at the hall
events.headline: Monster objects to music at the great hall
events.story: A monster living nearby has objected to the loud music at the great hall and has been visiting at night. Residents have decided to turn the volume down. A hero has been sent for.
chatter: No music at Heorot until the hero comes.
The monster does not like boomboxes.
A nice quiet week.

events.title: A wood on the move
events.headline: Wood seen advancing on the castle
events.story: Soldiers carrying branches have been reported marching on the castle, giving the impression that a wood is moving. Residents have found the sight unsettling. Couriers are avoiding the road.

why.carrier_delay_days: Couriers avoid the road.

chatter: The wood is moving. Plants are selling.

Parcels held outside the castle.

events.title: A letter fails to arrive
events.headline: Friar's message to Mantua goes astray
events.story: A friar's letter to a young man in Mantua has failed to arrive because of a quarantine. The consequences are said to be serious. The town has asked all couriers to check their rules.

why.demand.all: Gift buyers send flowers instead.
why.carrier_delay_days: A quarantine holds the mail.

chatter: The letter did not go through. Please do not send tragedy by post.

events.title: A love-juice mix-up
events.headline: Wrong lover anointed; wood in confusion
events.story: Mischief by a fairy with a flower has left four lovers each adoring the wrong person. Gifts are being sent to the wrong addresses. Shops are fielding a great many returns.

why.demand.all: A lot of gifts.

chatter: Wrong recipient on four orders.

events.title: A storm raised on purpose
events.headline: Magician raises storm; ship wrecked on his island
events.story: A magician on a distant island has raised a storm to bring his enemies ashore. A ship has been wrecked and passengers are on the beach. Couriers will not land until the weather clears.

why.demand.all: The island is busy.
why.carrier_delay_days: Ships will not land in a storm.

chatter: Storm on the island. Parcels held.

events.title: A bond falls due
events.headline: Merchant's bond falls due; payments in dispute
events.story: A merchant's ships have failed to return and a large bond has fallen due. A lender has asked for his pound of flesh, to the amazement of the court. Payment disputes in the city have risen.
events.source: The Merchant of Venice, William Shakespeare (c. 1597)
chatter: Two chargebacks, same merchant.
The bond is for money, not flesh.
Court is in session.

events.title: Twins mistaken for each other
events.headline: Twin brother and sister mistaken for each other; orders doubled
events.story: A pair of twins have been mistaken for each other throughout the town. Orders have been placed twice, once for each. Both claim they only ordered once.

why.demand.all: More orders, even if some are twins.

chatter: Two accounts, one person. Or is it?
Refund one of them.
The twin has apologised.

events.title: A long cold retreat
events.headline: Army retreats through snow; socks in short supply
events.story: An army is retreating through deep snow and the roads are impassable. Families in the capital are collecting warm things for the soldiers. Socks have been in short supply for weeks.

why.demand.all: People are collecting for the army.
why.demand.products.spare-sock: Warm feet.
why.carrier_delay_days: Roads blocked by snow.

chatter: Socks for the retreat. As many as we have.
Roads are impassable. Parcels held.
Please stop asking for gloves.

events.title: Facts, and only facts
events.headline: Board declares that only useful goods may be bought
events.story: The town council has resolved that only useful goods are to be bought in the borough. Ornaments are discouraged and imaginative products are viewed with suspicion. The shop has been asked to confirm which of its goods are facts.

why.demand.products.starter-puddle: A puddle is not a fact.
why.demand.products.pocket-jungle: A jungle is not a fact.

chatter: Facts only. The puddle is not useful.
The pen is a fact.
We have been inspected.

events.title: Three men pack for a boat trip
events.headline: Three men and a dog pack for a trip up the river
events.story: Three men and a dog have decided to take a boat trip up the river and have packed rather more than is sensible. A large order for food, bags and padding has come in. They say it will be a restful holiday.
events.source: Three Men in a Boat, Jerome K. Jerome (1889)
chatter: Three men and a dog. Large order.
They forgot the tin opener.
No one has done this properly yet.

events.title: A rider without a head
events.headline: Horseman without a head seen on the road at night
events.story: A rider with no head has been seen on the road after dark and couriers have declined to make night deliveries. Residents are looking for suitable head protection and a better lantern. The schoolmaster is said to have left.
events.source: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow, Washington Irving (1820)

why.carrier_delay_days: No deliveries after dark.

chatter: Do not deliver after dark. Rule of the week.
Helmets, because of the rider.
The rider does not need one.

events.title: A door in a wall
events.headline: Hidden garden door found after ten years
events.story: A girl has found a key and a door to a garden that has been locked for ten years. She has begun to tend it. Visitors say the garden is coming on well.
events.source: The Secret Garden, Frances Hodgson Burnett (1911)

why.demand.products.pocket-jungle: Everyone wants a garden of their own.
why.demand.products.starter-puddle: A bit of water for the plants.

chatter: A secret garden. Plants are moving.
Please mind the robin.
It is not a secret if it is on the news.

events.title: A gun club fires at the moon
events.headline: Gun club announces plan to fire a projectile at the moon
events.story: A club of gun enthusiasts has announced it will fire a projectile at the moon. A passenger has volunteered. Shops report heavy orders for padding.
events.source: From the Earth to the Moon, Jules Verne (1865)

why.demand.products.bubble-wrap: A passenger in a shell needs padding.

chatter: A gun club ordered forty rolls of wrap.
A passenger would like a helmet.
We do not do space.

events.title: Snowed in on the moor
events.headline: Moorland household snowed in for a week
events.story: A heavy snow has closed the moor road and left the Heights cut off. The household has not seen a visitor for a week. Parcels will arrive when the road is clear.

why.demand.products.spare-sock: Warm feet.
why.carrier_delay_days: Roads closed by snow.

chatter: Snow on the moor. Parcels held.
They have asked for sock and tin.
A ghost has asked to come in. We said no.

events.title: A fire at the hall
events.headline: Fire damages a country house; the household refurnishes
events.story: A fire in an upper room has damaged the hall. The household is refurnishing in a hurry and has asked for a great deal at once. Stationery and desk things are in demand.

why.demand.all: A big restocking.

chatter: Refurnishing order for the hall.
The attic is not on the list.
It is a very large order. Pay in advance.

events.title: A bachelor takes a house
events.headline: Wealthy bachelor takes a house nearby; families are interested
events.story: It is a truth universally acknowledged that a single man with a good fortune must be in want of a wife. A wealthy bachelor has taken a house near the village. The neighbouring families are buying gifts and new things to wear.

why.demand.all: Families are preparing to be seen.
why.demand.products.biscuit-tin: A tin is a good welcome gift.
why.demand.products.spare-sock: New things to wear.

chatter: A wealthy man has moved in. Orders are up.
Everyone wants a good impression.
A tin of biscuits, for a stranger.

events.title: A picnic on Box Hill
events.headline: Picnic party on the hill ends in disagreement
events.story: A party of friends has had a picnic on the hill that ended in a disagreement. Several have apologised since. Picnic orders have risen sharply as everyone wants to try again.

why.demand.products.emergency-sandwich: A fresh try at a picnic.

chatter: A picnic gone wrong. Sandwiches rising.
Please be nice to each other.
A cold drink is fine.

events.title: Four sisters give their breakfast away
events.headline: Four sisters give their Christmas breakfast to a hungry family
events.story: Four sisters have given their Christmas breakfast to a hungry family next door. Neighbours, moved, have sent gifts of their own. The village is in good spirits.

why.demand.all: A wave of generosity.
why.demand.products.spare-sock: Stocking fillers.

chatter: Gifts for the family next door. All sizes.
The sisters are good people.
Order for four. Plus a small one.
